previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer, recently found to have liver and bone metastases, was admitted for back pain and urinary incontinence. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection, which was treated with antibiotics, and MRI confirmed extensive osseous metastatic disease without spinal cord compression. Pain was managed with her home opioids and gabapentin. Radiation oncology recommended systemic therapy over radiation due to diffuse disease. She was transitioned to oral antibiotics, started on a bowel regimen due to chronic opioid use, and scheduled for port placement and oncology follow-up to initiate chemotherapy. She improved clinically, with resolution of incontinence and stable vital signs, and was discharged home in stable condition.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct

reexcision, she had breast conserving radiation administered at

In ___, a mammogram showed right breast 
microcalcifications
which were stable. These were in the retroareolar area. On the
left side, however, she had an asymmetry. This was superior and
posterior aspect of the breast and an ultrasound was performed
showing an ill-defined hypoechoic mass measuring about 1 cm. She
had a core biopsy of this area in ___. Pathology revealed
malignancy, so she underwent a left mastectomy, having had a
prior excision and radiation therapy on the left side. Final
surgical pathology showed invasive lobular cancer measuring 13
mm. This was histologic grade II. There was a single focus of
invasion. There was no lymphovascular invasion. Both hormone
receptors were positive while HER-2/neu was negative by
immunohistochemistry.  No lymph nodes were sampled given the
prior lower axillary dissection.

Her Oncotype recurrence score was 20. This corresponds to a 13%
___ risk of recurrence assuming ___ years of tamoxifen. We
would expect somewhat better results for management of lobular
carcinoma with an aromatase inhibitor. On the other hand, this
was apparently recurrent disease after prior radiation therapy,
which might have diminished tumor sensitivity to additional
therapy.

We discussed adjuvant treatment, both endocrine therapy and
chemo-endocrine therapy. She favored endocrine therapy alone
strongly and I felt this was an acceptable choice. Accordingly,
anastrozole was started in ___.

She recently presented to the ED on ___ with nausea,
vomiting, and abdominal pain. This was felt to be related to her
gastroparesis. Her CT abdomen/pelvis returned consistent with
numerous hepatic and osseous metastases. In the hospital, she
underwent a liver biopsy which revealed a carcinoma compatible
with a breast primary tumor. Estrogen receptor was positive. 
HER-2/neu was not assessed.
